title: Consistent hashing moves only 1/n of keys when a node joins
body: Hashing keys and servers onto a ring and assigning each key to the next server clockwise means adding one server only steals keys from its single neighbour's arc, about a 1/n share. Caches stopped reshuffling the world at every membership change. Karger and colleagues published it in 1997 for Akamai's web caching problem.
source_hint: Karger et al., 'Consistent Hashing and Random Trees' (1997)
